facts.text: Motor City Dubai houses the Dubai Autodrome, a 4.5‑km race track that hosts international motorsport events.
Motor City was originally conceived as part of the 2003 Dubailand entertainment complex, a $64.3 billion vision that would span 278 km².
The Dubailand project, including Motor City, was paused in 2008 after the financial crisis but restarted in 2013 with $55 billion raised.
Motor City sits within the Attractions & Experience World zone of Dubailand, one of six themed “worlds” planned for the complex.
Motor City’s development was overseen by Tatweer, a Dubai Holding subsidiary, before being taken over by Dubai Properties Group.
By 2025, several Dubailand projects, including those in Motor City, were slated to open, marking a revival of the original vision.
